chunks: From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Ibrahim al-Karkhi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I said to him, 'I am able to face the Qibla while in the mount.' He said, 'What is this narrowness? Do you not have a model in the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family)?'

key_terms.أُسْوَةٌ: Model or example, specifically referring to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family)
key_terms.الْقِبْلَةِ: The Qibla, the direction of prayer towards the Kaaba in Mecca
key_terms.الْمَحْمِلِ: The mount or vehicle (e.g., camel, car) in which one is traveling

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on facing the Qibla while praying in a moving vehicle according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) critiques the companion's excessive rigor (tadayyun) regarding facing the Qibla while traveling in a mount, invoking the Prophet as the ultimate model (uswah) of ease. This hadith highlights the Shia scholarly principle that prophetic practice often accommodates practical necessities, discouraging unnecessary strictness in religious observance. It underscores the balance between reverence for the Qibla and the flexibility granted during travel, reflecting the broader juristic concept of 'ease in difficulty'.
